title: Slips, Trips & Good Housekeeping
whatItIs: HSE says around 1,000 slips and trips a year on construction sites cause broken bones or dislocations. Many happen because something is in the way.

keyFacts.text: Every part of a site MUST be kept in good order, and work areas reasonably clean.
Timber with projecting nails MUST NOT be used or left lying where it could hurt someone.
There MUST be safe access to and from every place of work on site, so far as reasonably practicable.
Sites, approaches and traffic routes MUST have suitable and sufficient lighting.

keyFacts: Everyone is responsible: don't leave cables across corridors or waste in stairwells.
Don't let stored materials spread onto footpaths, access routes or escape routes.

visual.caption: Main causes of slips and trips on site, and the fix (HSG150)

rows: Materials and waste left lying around
Keep areas tidy; use marked waste areas, bins and skips
Use cordless tools; run cables at high level
Uneven, muddy, wet or icy walkways
Level ruts, stone mud, grit ice; wear good-grip footwear
Soundly built temporary ramps, e.g. at doorways

a.label: Storage areas
points: Marked areas for plant, materials and waste
Deliveries planned to keep stock on site low

b.label: Walkways and stairs
points: Kept clear of obstructions at all times
No materials or waste left in them

onTheTest.question: Extension leads for temporary lighting run along a busy corridor. What is the best way to stop trips?
options: Tape the leads flat to the floor
Put a warning sign at each end
Run the leads at high level along the corridor
Tell everyone to watch where they walk
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 504: run cables for temporary lighting or mains tools at high level, especially along corridors.

onTheTest.question: According to HSE, what causes many slips and trips on construction sites?
options: Something in the way, such as materials or waste
onTheTest.why: HSE: around 1,000 slips and trips a year on sites cause fractures or dislocations. Many happen simply because something, such as materials or waste, is in the way.

traps: Small changes in level trip people too, not just big obstacles.
Floor protection sheets can create a slip or trip risk themselves.
Take extra care to keep the foot of stairs and ladders clear and in good condition.
Housekeeping isn't only the labourer's job: everyone manages their own waste.
